Define a distribution for the moments of its order statistics

Source: R/os_dist.R
os_dist.Rd

Builds the distribution object that os_moments takes in its dist argument, from the distribution function, the density and the quantile function of a continuous distribution. The object describes the standard member of a location-scale family: os_moments() computes the moments for this member and applies its own location and scale arguments afterwards. A user who wants a \(t_5\) distribution with location 3 and scale 2 supplies the \(t_5\) functions here and passes location = 3, scale = 2 to os_moments().

Usage

os_dist(
  p,
  d,
  q,
  support = c(-Inf, Inf),
  symmetric = FALSE,
  tail = c(Inf, Inf),
  name = "user"
)

Arguments

p

The distribution function, with the signature of R's p* functions: p(q, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE), vectorized in q. The log.p and lower.tail arguments must be honored, because the integrands are evaluated on the log scale in both tails.

d

The density, d(x, log = FALSE), vectorized in x, with log honored.

q

The quantile function, q(p), vectorized in p.

support

Numeric vector of length two, the endpoints of the support, finite or infinite. They are the limits of integration.

symmetric

Logical. TRUE if the density is symmetric about its median, that is \(Q(1 - u) = 2 Q(1/2) - Q(u)\). A symmetric distribution lets os_moments() halve the number of double integrals of a full matrix and check the reflection symmetry of its result.

tail

Numeric vector of length two, the tail indices \((\nu_L, \nu_U)\): the density decays like \(|x|^{-\nu_L - 1}\) in the lower tail and like \(x^{-\nu_U - 1}\) in the upper tail. Inf for a tail that decays faster than any power, or for a bounded tail. The indices decide which moments exist (see Details).

name

A label for printing.

Value

An object of class "os_dist": a list with the components name, p, d, q, support, symmetric, tail, center (the median \(Q(1/2)\)) and closed (the closed-form moments the distribution has, none for a user distribution).

Details

The moment condition. For a parent whose density decays like \(|x|^{-\nu - 1}\), the density of \(X_{(r)}\) decays like \(|x|^{-\nu r - 1}\) below and like \(x^{-\nu (n - r + 1) - 1}\) above, so \(E|X_{(r)}|^k < \infty\) if and only if \(\nu_L r > k\) and \(\nu_U (n - r + 1) > k\). os_moments() applies this condition with \(k = 2\) to every requested rank and refuses a moment that does not exist. A Cauchy parent, tail = c(1, 1), has a median of five with a finite variance and extremes without a mean.

Accuracy requirement. The log-tails p(x, log.p = TRUE) and p(x, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE) must keep relative precision deep in both tails, as R's base distributions do. A function that computes log(p(x)) from an underflowing probability loses the tail, and the integrals with it. os_dist() checks that the three functions honor their arguments at the median and are vectorized, and that d integrates to \(1/2\) between the quartiles, where p rises by \(1/2\). os_moments() checks that the log-tails and the log-density are finite at the median and at the split points of the smallest and the largest requested rank, and that the density of every order statistic it integrates has mass 1. None of these certifies accuracy.

Location limit. The integrals are taken about the median of the standard member, and the integration range is split in units of its spread (its interquartile range), so the scale on which the standard member is supplied does not matter: the package's tests check a normal supplied with standard deviations from \(10^{-3}\) to \(10^6\). Its location does: a standard member whose own location is large, say \(10^8\) with unit scale, loses the digits of \(x - Q(1/2)\) in double precision and the computation stops with an error. Supply the standard member and pass the location to os_moments() instead, which also keeps os_blue() exact.

Common parents. Each function wraps the corresponding stats function with its shape fixed and passes lower.tail, log.p and log by name, as in the examples. The declarations that differ between parents are these.

Parentsupporttail
Student \(t_\nu\) (pt, dt, qt), symmetricc(-Inf, Inf)c(nu, nu)
gamma (pgamma, dgamma, qgamma)c(0, Inf)c(Inf, Inf)
Weibull (pweibull, dweibull, qweibull)c(0, Inf)c(Inf, Inf)
lognormal (plnorm, dlnorm, qlnorm)c(0, Inf)c(Inf, Inf)
beta (pbeta, dbeta, qbeta)c(0, 1)c(Inf, Inf)

The lognormal tail decays faster than any power, so every moment exists. A distribution declared on c(-Inf, Inf) whose density is zero below some point stops with an error that its log-tail is not finite, which is the sign that support is missing.

See also

os_moments

Examples

# Student t with 5 degrees of freedom: tail index 5 in both tails
t5 <- os_dist(function(q, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)
                stats::pt(q, df = 5, lower.tail = lower.tail, log.p = log.p),
              function(x, log = FALSE) stats::dt(x, df = 5, log = log),
              function(p) stats::qt(p, df = 5),
              symmetric = TRUE, tail = c(5, 5), name = "t5")
os_moments(5, dist = t5)
#> Exact moments of order statistics: t5 (location 0, scale 1), n = 5, ranks 1 2 3 4 5
#> alpha (means):
#>            r1            r2            r3            r4            r5 
#> -1.450975e+00 -5.580065e-01 -8.649563e-18  5.580065e-01  1.450975e+00 
#> B (covariance matrix):
#>           r1        r2        r3        r4        r5
#> r1 1.1478770 0.3802510 0.2288315 0.1665120 0.1398297
#> r2 0.3802510 0.4270062 0.2648562 0.1959689 0.1665120
#> r3 0.2288315 0.2648562 0.3501660 0.2648562 0.2288315
#> r4 0.1665120 0.1959689 0.2648562 0.4270062 0.3802510
#> r5 0.1398297 0.1665120 0.2288315 0.3802510 1.1478770
#> route: integrate; quadrature error estimate: 2.17e-10
#> checks: reflection 1.61e-17; identities sum_alpha 2.94e-17, sum_sq 8.88e-16, sum_B 3.29e-14

# The Cauchy: the median of five has a variance, the extremes have no mean
cauchy <- os_dist(stats::pcauchy, stats::dcauchy, stats::qcauchy,
                  symmetric = TRUE, tail = c(1, 1), name = "cauchy")
os_moments(5, ranks = 3, dist = cauchy)
#> Exact moments of order statistics: cauchy (location 0, scale 1), n = 5, ranks 3
#> alpha (means):
#>            r3 
#> -1.028762e-17 
#> B (covariance matrix):
#>          r3
#> r3 1.221253
#> route: integrate; quadrature error estimate: 3.89e-14
#> checks: reflection 1.39e-17; identities n/a

# A gamma with shape 2: a semi-bounded support, every moment finite
gamma2 <- os_dist(function(q, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)
                    stats::pgamma(q, shape = 2, lower.tail = lower.tail, log.p = log.p),
                  function(x, log = FALSE) stats::dgamma(x, shape = 2, log = log),
                  function(p) stats::qgamma(p, shape = 2),
                  support = c(0, Inf), name = "gamma2")
os_moments(10, ranks = c(1, 5, 10), dist = gamma2, scale = 3)
#> Exact moments of order statistics: gamma2 (location 0, scale 3), n = 10, ranks 1 5 10
#> alpha (means):
#>        r1        r5       r10 
#>  1.398065  4.725263 13.868870 
#> B (covariance matrix):
#>            r1        r5        r10
#> r1  0.6842539 0.3962219  0.2986211
#> r5  0.3962219 2.0064850  1.5292810
#> r10 0.2986211 1.5292810 20.0825000
#> route: integrate; quadrature error estimate: 1.11e-10
#> checks: reflection n/a; identities n/a
